page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Margin notes stand in the right margin, beside the lines they annotate. Printed page number 37 at the top right, running head centred above the text, gathering signature "C 3" at the foot.

main_text.p: tiorem facit, frumentum uti pararent: tri* duoq; proximo iter pronunciat. Sed Iordanis, flumen validissimum, transitu prohibebat: quia neq; navium copia pro tempore erat, neq; vadari fluvius poterat, qui tum pleno alveo ferebatur. Igitur arcam Iosue,3. præferri a sacerdotibus, eosdemq; adverso flumine consistere jubet. Quo facto, incisus Iordanis traditur: ita per siccum copiæ traductę. Erat in his locis opidum, no-Hiericho. mine Hiericho, muris validissimis munitum, neq; expugnationi neque obsidioni facile. Iosue 6. Sed Iesus Domino fretus, non armis aut viribus urbem aggressus, ferri arcam Dei circa muros iubet: sacerdotes q; præire arcam & tuba canere. Sed cum arca septies circulata esset, muri ac turres conciderunt: direptum oppidum atq; incensum. Tum Iesus Dominum traditur {a}. In-Defunt de adversus Gæ ductus exercitus: locatisq; quedam. a tergo urbis infidiis, Iesus metum simu-Vide notas. las terga hosti dedit. Quo viso qui in oppido erant patentibus portis cedentibus intare. Ita si qui infidiis fuerant, vacuam urbem ceperunt: cæsiq; omnes absque ullius effugio. Rex captus, summoq; supplicio affectus. Quod ubi vicinarum gentium

page.notes: Handwritten marginal annotation "XL-II" at the lower right, beside "gentium", not transcribed as it is not printed. The "{a}" mark after "traditur" is a small superscript letter in the text; no note carrying the letter "a" is clearly printed, and the note "Defunt" is placed beside its line. The word "tri*" carries a printed mark after "tri" that I could not identify with certainty. The word "fimu-" is read as "simu-" from context ("simulas"); the first letter is doubtful. "infidiis" is copied as printed in both places. The line "intare" is read as printed; the correct word is probably "intrare" and is left as printed.
